chunks: And to you, O servants of Allah,

that a believer does not pass the morning or the evening except that his soul is suspect in his eyes, so he should continually visit it and ask it to increase (in good), so be like those who preceded you and those who passed before you, they dismantled the world as a traveler dismantles (his camp), and covered it as distances are covered.
ai.seo_question: How should a believer view and treat their own soul according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) exhorts believers to be distrustful of their own souls (nafs), constantly scrutinizing and encouraging them to increase in good deeds. He urges them to emulate the predecessors who treated the world as a transient passage, leaving it behind like a traveler leaving a camp.

en.sayed-ali-raza: You should know, O creatures of Allāh,

that a believer should be distrustful of his heart every morning and evening. He should always blame it (for shortcomings) and ask it to add to (its good acts). You should behave like those who have gone before you and the precedents in front of you. They left this world like a traveller and covered it as distance is covered.
